6-8 Science Curriculum Pilot Process
Discussion on COVID-19

publicComments.name: Whitney Glockner-Black
publicComments.summary: Raised concerns about students accessing inappropriate content on YouTube via school devices and urged the district to implement stronger content restrictions quickly.

publicComments.name: Katherine Stewart
publicComments.summary: Stated she does not want her child back in school until a vaccine is available, preferring the inconvenience of distance learning over the risk of death.

publicComments.name: Michelle Gagliardi
publicComments.summary: As a parent of a kindergartner in an SDC class, opposed returning to in-person learning because her son cannot wear a mask or social distance, and argued that students with disabilities face greater health risks.

publicComments.name: Mercedes Kwiatowski
publicComments.summary: As a psychiatrist in the community, expressed support for cautiously moving toward in-person learning given the mental health toll on children, while emphasizing teacher involvement in the planning process.

publicComments.name: Kristi Herrera
publicComments.summary: As a kindergarten teacher, strongly opposed returning to campus before the end of the first trimester, citing safety concerns about young children wearing masks, the disruption of existing teacher-student bonds, and the complications of shuffling staff and students.

publicComments.name: Sandy Hoover
publicComments.summary: As a TK/K teacher in a high-risk group, described the unavoidable close physical contact with young students involving bodily fluids, inadequate PPE, and the impossible choice between risking COVID infection or losing her income.

publicComments.name: Kerri Yen
publicComments.summary: As a parent of a kindergartner with an IEP for speech, supported returning younger students to in-person learning as soon as possible, noting that distance learning is driving inequity and that some families are already leaving RCSD for alternatives.

publicComments.name: Cameron Hoffman
publicComments.summary: As a parent of two district students, supported both teacher safety and in-person instruction for the most vulnerable learners, urging the district to learn from neighboring schools already reopening and to do everything possible for students with the greatest needs.

publicComments.name: Allison Oldford
publicComments.summary: As a parent of first graders currently in a safe childcare group setting, expressed support for a return to in-person instruction while also respecting teacher concerns, arguing the two positions are not at odds.

publicComments.name: Brian Crawford
publicComments.summary: As a parent of three district children, shared that his son's mental health has deteriorated significantly during distance learning and urged the board to continue working proactively with teachers to return to campus as soon as safely possible.

publicComments.name: Janelle Allen
publicComments.summary: As an immunocompromised parent of a kindergartner, opposed the plan to bring students back at the end of October and urged the board to wait until flu season is over, arguing online learning better preserves existing teacher-student bonds.

publicComments.name: Jennifer Wenzel
publicComments.summary: As an RCSD teacher of 13 years and mother of a toddler, opposed reopening given Redwood City's high COVID infection rate, children's higher viral load, and the risk of bringing the virus home to family members.

publicComments.name: Jeanette Serrano
publicComments.summary: As a 34-year kindergarten teacher, opposed returning TK-1 students to campus while the county is still in the 'substantial' red tier, citing the inability of young children to maintain masks or distancing and her own plans to seek a medical exemption.

publicComments.name: Sarah Latora
publicComments.summary: If returning to in-person, preferred Option 1 (AM/PM cohorts with cleaning between) over Option 2, raised concerns about funding for cleaning, and praised Clifford Elementary staff for their excellent distance learning.

publicComments.name: Susan Forquer
publicComments.summary: As a parent of first and second graders at Adelante Selby, strongly opposed moving students out of dual immersion programs during any return to school and urged a separate survey asking immersion families whether they would prefer to remain in distance learning to preserve language acquisition.

publicComments.name: Eric Sutton
publicComments.summary: As a parent of a first grader who is thriving in his current distance learning classroom, opposed disrupting existing student-teacher relationships mid-semester and expressed frustration at the prospect of students being reshuffled.
